title: Christ as both judgment and mercy at the place of burnt offering
english: In the place where burnt offerings are offered, they will kill the sin offering. That same place is fire—Christ is both judgment and propitiation.
translator_notes: True OET: no ANF; do not copy Barkley FOTC 83.
orientation: Origen is explaining the Levitical rule about where the sin offering is killed, applying it spiritually to Christ.

title: Holy things eaten within
english: It is holy of holies; let it be eaten in the court (Leviticus 6:26). Not to scatter holy teachings outside. To eat within the church.
translator_notes: True OET: no ANF; do not copy Barkley FOTC 83.
orientation: Origen is explaining the rule that the sin offering is most holy and must be eaten in the court, applying it to the church's teaching.

title: Contact with Christ sanctifies, contact with sin pollutes
english: Everyone who touches its flesh will be sanctified (Leviticus 6:27). Contact with Christ sanctifies; contact with sin pollutes.
translator_notes: True OET: no ANF; do not copy Barkley FOTC 83.
orientation: Origen is explaining the rule about eating the sin offering in the court, applying it to the soul's contact with Christ and with sin.

title: Washing the blood-stained garment in the holy place
english: If blood has been sprinkled on a garment, you shall wash it in the holy place (Leviticus 6:27). A stain is washed away by prayer and tears.
translator_notes: True OET: no ANF; do not copy Barkley FOTC 83.
orientation: Origen is interpreting Leviticus 6:27 about contact with sacrificial blood, now applying the rule about blood sprinkled on a garment to the cleansing of the soul.

title: Vessels of clay and bronze
english: A clay vessel will be broken; a bronze one will be scoured. The fragility of the flesh; the strength of correction. Vessels for honor.
translator_notes: True OET: no ANF; do not copy Barkley FOTC 83.
orientation: Origen is interpreting the vessels used in the sin offering, applying them to the soul's fragility and the discipline that purifies it.

title: Unleavened sincerity
english: It shall not be cooked with leaven. Purge out the leaven of malice. Be the unleavened bread of sincerity.
translator_notes: True OET: no ANF; do not copy Barkley FOTC 83.
orientation: Origen is applying the rules for the grain offering to the moral life of the believer, moving from the broken vessel and scoured bronze to the command about leaven.

title: The priest who offers eats; the minister lives by the gospel
english: The priest who offers it shall eat it (Leviticus 6:26). He who ministers the word, let him live from the gospel (1 Corinthians 9:14). Not a hireling but a shepherd (John 10:12).
translator_notes: True OET: no ANF; do not copy Barkley FOTC 83.
orientation: Origen is applying the Levitical rule about who may eat the sacrifice to Christian ministers, contrasting the true pastor with the hireling.

title: Who may eat the holy things
english: Every male of the priestly kind shall eat it (Leviticus 6:18). The male is a strong sense, not a dissolute affection. Holy things for holy people.
translator_notes: True OET: no ANF; do not copy Barkley FOTC 83.
orientation: Origen is explaining the rule about who may eat the priestly portion, interpreting 'male' spiritually as the strong mind rather than weak emotion.

title: Contact with the altar sanctifies
english: Whatever touches the altar will be made holy. The altar is Christ; the contact is of faith. Draw near to the living stone (1 Peter 2:4).
translator_notes: True OET: no ANF; do not copy Barkley FOTC 83.
orientation: Origen is explaining the Levitical rule that whatever touches the altar becomes holy, applying it to Christ as the living stone whom believers touch by faith.

title: The Ram of the Hidden Fault
english: The law of the ram for a fault is a holy of holies. A hidden fault seeks light. By the ram Christ sets free.
translator_notes: True OET: no ANF; do not copy Barkley FOTC 83.
orientation: Origen is explaining the Levitical offering of a ram for a hidden fault, reading it as a figure of Christ.

title: Sacrifice of praise with oiled cakes
english: A sacrifice of praise with cakes and oil. Eucharist—an act of thanksgiving. Sing to the Lord (Psalm 96:1).
translator_notes: True OET: no ANF; do not copy Barkley FOTC 83.
orientation: Origen is interpreting the Levitical offerings spiritually, moving from the ram of the fault offering to the sacrifice of praise and the Eucharist.

title: All fat belongs to the Lord
english: All the fat belongs to the Lord; you shall not eat it (Leviticus 3:16). The richness of glory belongs to God. A heart rich in mercy. Amen.
translator_notes: True OET: no ANF; do not copy Barkley FOTC 83.
orientation: Origen is concluding his spiritual reading of the sacrifice of praise, applying the Levitical rule about fat to the soul's richest devotion.
